Why our database migration took three tries

The first attempt failed because we had not accounted for a foreign key that the ORM created implicitly; the second attempt ran out of disk space halfway through the rewrite of a two hundred gigabyte table on the primary.

The third attempt succeeded only after we switched to a two-phase approach: backfill the new column in batches of ten thousand rows, verify counts, then flip the application reads over.

Looking back, the lesson is boring but true: migrations that rewrite large tables need a rollback story that has actually been rehearsed, not one that only exists in a design document.
